summary:
Trends and hitting are the categories to trust across the board today — every rating shows 8-2 (80%, n=10) over the last 14 days in both buckets, well above season baselines sitting in the 50-56% range. Runs is right behind at 70-80% depending on rating, with R2 runs leading the pack at 8-2 (80%, n=10) versus a 53% season mark. Bullpen fatigue remains the one category to fade across every rating — flat 5-5 (50%, n=10) with a 4-game losing streak model-wide, and a season mark under .500 at 46-47%. The combo data backs this up: trends+sp (57.9%, n=637) and trends+runs (57.2%, n=704) are the two sturdiest category pairings all year, so any pick where trends lines up with either sp or runs deserves extra confidence tonight.

With just one game on the board, this is a clean, concentrated spot. All four ratings converge on MIL over TBR, with deltas clustered tight between -2.16 and -2.62 — that kind of unanimous consensus across R1-R4 is exactly the signal type that's been hot lately. MIL also happens to be the single best team-when-liked play in the sample: 50-23 (68%, n=73) overall and 28-13 (68%, +16.0u) specifically on strong plays, the highest-volume team on the board and consistently profitable. TBR as the opponent isn't a soft fade either — they're 44-19 (70%, n=63) when the model backs them, so this isn't a case of the model leaning against a live dog, it's picking the Brewers straight through a quality opponent. R2 is the rating to lean hardest on here: it's running hot across trends, runs, and hitting (all 80%) and posted the best recent strong-play stretch of any rating, 6-1 (86%, +3.0u) over the last 14 days and 10-4 (71%, +6.0u) over 30. With Misiorowski on the mound and every rating stacking the same direction, this is a high-conviction single-game night — the only yellow flag is bullpen_fatigue dragging down an otherwise clean board, so weight that category down if it diverges from the consensus pick.
